extracted.intended_audience: educated general readers interested in biblical criticism, deism, and historical/textual analysis
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and evidential signs used to judge the authenticity, authorship, dating, and reliability of biblical books (internal consistency, historical references, linguistic markers, numeric accuracy, stylistic unity, etc.). Drawn from Thomas Paine's Age of Reason commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contemporaneous historical mention
rubrics_metrics.description: If those prophets, as they are called, were men of such importance in their day... how can it be accounted for that not one of those histories should say anything about them?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether persons/authors claimed to be important are mentioned in contemporaneous histories (e.g., Kings and Chronicles). Absence of mention despite chronological overlap is evidence against claimed prominence or authenticity; Paine illustrates this with a table showing many prophets not mentioned in Kings/Chronicles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chronological/internal dating consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: The passage in Genesis refers itself for time to Chronicles; the book of Chronicles ... was not begun to be written until at least eight hundred and sixty years after the time of Moses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use internal cross-references and genealogies to test whether claimed authorship/dating is possible. If one book clearly postdates another but the earlier is claimed to be original, that inconsistency undermines traditional attributions (example: verses in Genesis matching 1 Chronicles imply later composition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Textual duplication and misplaced verses
rubrics_metrics.description: What kind of cutting and shuffling has it been that the first three verses in Ezra should be the last two verses in 2 Chronicles, or that the last two in 2 Chronicles should be the first three in Ezra?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify verbatim repeats or passages appearing in different books/locations; such duplication suggests compilation, cut-and-paste editing, or ignorance by compilers rather than single-author composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative completeness and coherence
rubrics_metrics.description: The last verse in Chronicles is broken abruptly... Another instance occurs in Joshua v. ... the story ends, and the chapter too. Either this story is broken off in the middle, or it is a story told by some Jewish humourist ... and the compilers ... have told it as a serious matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether episodes/stories have coherent beginnings, middles, and ends. Abrupt breaks, unresolved episodes, or senseless passages indicate poor compilation, later corruption, or non-serious/fragmentary origins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerical consistency and accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: In Ezra ii. ... the whole congregation together was forty and two thousand three hundred and threescore. But whoever will take the trouble of casting up the several particulars, will find that the total is but 29,818; so that the error is 12,542.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify arithmetical totals against listed particulars. Large errors in census/enrolment totals signal unreliability in the text and undermine claims of exactness or divine inspiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stylistic and thematic coherence (single-author unity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whoever will take the trouble of reading the book ascribed to Isaiah, will find it one of the most wild and disorderly compositions ever put together; it has neither beginning, middle, nor end... except a short historical part... is one continued incoherent, bombastical rant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a work displays consistent style, theme, and organization consistent with single authorship. Fragmentary, incoherent, or wildly varying sections suggest multiple authors, later additions, or compilation from loose essays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anachronism and mention of later events
rubrics_metrics.description: The latter part of the 44th chapter, and the beginning of the 45th, so far from having been written by Isaiah, could only have been written by some person who lived at least an hundred and fifty years after Isaiah was dead... a compliment to Cyrus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for explicit references to persons, events, or decrees that postdate the purported author (e.g., Isaiah praising Cyrus). Such anachronisms are strong evidence of later composition or interpolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linguistic and cultural origin markers
rubrics_metrics.description: The astronomical names, Pleiades, Orion, and Arcturus, are Greek and not Hebrew names, and it does not appear from any thing that is to be found in the Bible that the Jews knew any thing of astronomy...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze vocabulary, proper names, and cultural references for language-origin signals (Greek vs Hebrew names, translated terms). Presence of non-native lexical items or untranslated foreign names indicates translation from other languages or non-native authorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical/contextual relevance to claimed author/time
rubrics_metrics.description: Some [Psalms] are moral, and others are very revengeful; and the greater part relates to certain local circumstances of the Jewish nation at the time they were written... The 137th Psalm could not have been written till more than 400 years after the time of David.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether content reflects events, circumstances, or perspectives consistent with the life/time of the ascribed author. Later historical allusions within a text undermine traditional dating and attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship attribution and pseudepigraphy
rubrics_metrics.description: The book of Genesis, though it is placed first in the Bible, and ascribed to Moses, has been manufactured by some unknown person... The compilers ... picked up some loose, anonymous essays, and put them together under the names of such authors as best suited their purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Question putative author attributions when internal evidence (style, chronology, thematic fit) contradicts them. Pseudonymous ascription and later compilers assigning famous names is a recurring pattern to watch for.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual/cultural correspondence between content and purported authors' milieu
rubrics_metrics.description: The book of Job carries no internal evidence of being an Hebrew book; the genius of the composition... are not Hebrew; that it has been translated from another language into Hebrew, and that the author of the book was a Gentile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare the scientific, philosophical, or cultural knowledge displayed in a text with what is known of the claimed author's community. Discrepancies (e.g., advanced natural philosophy in a text attributed to an allegedly ignorant people) suggest foreign origin or later insertion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prophetic formulation vagueness / built-in escape clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: In his metaphor of the potter and the clay ... he guards his prognostications in such a crafty manner as always to leave himself a door to escape by... 'if that nation... turn from their evil, I will repent me of the evil that I thought to do unto them.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether prophetic statements are framed so broadly or conditionally that they cannot be falsified. Vague or conditional prophecies function as anti-patterns for genuine prophecy because they protect the prophet from being proven wrong.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composite compilation evidence (mixing different authors and epochs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The compilers of the Bible mixed and confounded the writings of different authors with each other; which alone... is sufficient to destroy the authenticity of an compilation, because it is more than presumptive evidence that the compilers are ignorant who the authors were.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify shifts in tone, repeated insertions, duplicate passages, and chronological contradictions that indicate the text is a composite of multiple authors and redactional layers rather than a single coherent original work.
